Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m starting with `README.md` as required. I’ll then use the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this task changes the dogfish target policy and requires keyframe evidence before controller edits.

The workspace has four sampled solver entries, all reporting the same `left_domain` score, so duplicate-result detection matters here. I’m anchoring the visual review in the guidance, observations, metrics, candidate sources, and inherited optimizer notes before deciding whether those samples are genuinely independent evidence.

The four sampled keyframe sheets are byte-identical despite three different policy-file hashes, and their metrics match exactly except wall time. Visually, the controller makes a productive leftward closing leg but never reaches the developed cylinder wakes; it then pitches sharply nose-up and exits the upper boundary. I’m checking the policy diffs and inherited notes now to identify which parameter variations were behaviorally inert and what structural mechanism has not yet been tested.

The assigned parent’s inherited evaluation supplies the decisive new negative result: gating the previously harmful lateral-velocity correction until deep rearward dual-opening did preserve the `6.609L` closest approach, but still produced the identical upper exit while worsening upstream travel, mean/final range, progress, and score. I’m treating that as the informative failure against the sampled `0.10/0.65` anchor and inspecting its released sheet before selecting the next mechanism.

The evidence now rules out both joint-allocation tuning and body-lateral-velocity correction, even when the latter is restricted to confirmed course loss. I’m recording a single new hypothesis before touching the solver: preserve the exact closing law, then smoothly reverse—not merely attenuate—the bounded steering request only under the already-tested deep-rearward dual-opening gate. This isolates whether late counter-curvature can break the upper-return topology without sacrificing the approach.

The candidate and both required evidence files are now updated. The durable lesson records the inherited gated lateral-velocity test as a concrete negative result; the solver adds only one owned parameter and keeps the evaluated approach unchanged whenever the recovery gate is zero. I’m invoking the required checker now, starting with the semantic guidance/provenance check.

The required semantic check found a rendered-workspace metadata defect: `README.md` lists the same copied parent twice, so it cannot resolve a unique assigned parent. I’m removing only that duplicate marker line, then rerunning the check; the task contract and evidence list remain unchanged.

The semantic check now passes after resolving the duplicate parent marker. I’m continuing the same required checker with the non-CFD Julia contract/schema test, followed separately by the editable-boundary audit.

The Julia check could not start because `julia` is absent from this runner’s `PATH` (exit 127); the policy itself did not execute or fail. I’m checking the workspace and standard tool locations for an available Julia binary before treating that as an environment limitation.

The boundary audit passes. No Julia executable exists in the workspace or searched standard locations, so the mandated runtime contract command remains unavailable in this environment; I’m compensating with the checker’s deterministic schema validation plus an explicit static field/reference audit, then doing a final diff review without running CFD.

Produced exactly one Phase 2 policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl) preserves the sampled closing controller and reverses its bounded steering request only during confirmed deep-rearward range opening.
- Added visual diagnosis and falsification criteria to [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md).
- Added the inherited gated lateral-velocity correction as a concrete negative lesson in [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md).

Guidance/provenance and boundary checks pass; all 23 referenced parameter fields are declared. The Julia runtime check could not execute because Julia is unavailable in the environment. No CFD was run.
